title: Disparities are easier to identify than explain: an evidence and gap map of police outcomes research
abstract: Objectives To systematically map global evidence on disparities in police outcomes and identify evidence concentrations, gaps, and methodological limitations. Methods An evidence and gap map was developed using systematic searches of the Global Policing Database. Eligible studies ( n = 554; 1999–2021) were screened, coded, and classified by characteristics such as police actions, explanatory approaches, and methodological characteristics. Results The evidence base has expanded rapidly but is heavily concentrated on racial disparities in the United States and a small number of highly visible police actions. Theoretical development and evidence synthesis have not kept pace with the growth of primary research: more than half of studies lacked an explicit theoretical framework, and all six eligible evidence syntheses were judged critically low confidence using AMSTAR-2. Conclusions Research has been more successful at documenting disparities than explaining them. Stronger theory, causal inference, rigorous benchmarking, and higher-quality evidence synthesis are needed to strengthen evidence informing policing policy and practice.
